data.plain: Formal clause: `not_proven(P)` does not imply `proven(not P)`; coverage is closed-world only inside declared finite domains.

analogy.boundary: The drawer only works as an example because it is small and was searched completely; it says nothing about rooms nobody searched.

maps.analogy: the one drawer you searched all the way through
maps.doctrine: the declared finite domain, checked completely

maps.analogy: the rest of the house you have not checked

analogy.text: Not finding your keys in one drawer tells you they are not in that drawer. It tells you nothing about the rest of the house.

reader.counterexample: A status page reports a property as clean because a scan returned no findings, without ever stating what the scan covered, so silence over an unbounded space is read as safety.
reader.does_not_prove: Recording known gaps says nothing about gaps nobody has thought to declare.

example.text: The self-ignorance coverage ledger records the difference between what has been declared in scope and what has actually been written down, and does not allow an unmapped area to be read as empty; the gap stays recorded so it can be filled in later.

reader.governs: Whether an absence of evidence may count as a negative result, and within what scope.
reader.plain: Finding no evidence for something differs from showing it is false. You can call an absence a "no" only inside a list you have checked completely; otherwise the honest answer is "unknown".
reader.potential_misread: That no evidence means no problem, when outside a fully checked list it means the answer is not yet known.
reader.refuses: Treating absence of evidence as evidence of absence.
reader.requires: A declared finite domain, checked completely, before any conclusion from absence; outside it, an unshown claim is recorded as unknown.
reader.why_it_matters: "We did not see a problem" stays separate from "there is no problem", which is how unnoticed failures get signed off.

data.statement:
Formal clause: `not_proven(P)` does not imply `proven(not P)`; coverage is
closed-world only inside declared finite domains.

Lineage: open-world assumption, bounded closed-world assumption, soundness
versus completeness.

Route: recorded as strongly witnessed by `self_ignorance_coverage_ledger` and
`doctrine_fact_claim_audit`. Both record the gaps between what was declared and
what has been built, and leave everything outside the declared domains marked
unknown.

Anti-axiom: finding no evidence of something shows it is absent.
